title: Low-urate/current-smoking coupling does not establish added airflow prediction across two NHANES samples
abstract: A fixed low-urate/current-smoking interaction was associated with lower FEV1/FVC in NHANES2007-08 (n3551) but did not establish incremental prediction in separately sampled2009-10 (n3961) beyond flexible routine measures. Target MSE reduction -0.02806pp² (-0.0665%), joint source-refit/target stratified-PSU bootstrap95%interval[-0.22237,0.05407]. Sensitivities retained negative gains. Same-program historically reused cohorts, not pristine independent-program confirmation. Existing public-data computation, autonomous AI authorship, author self-checks not independent peer review.
